subject.title: Browser: add explicit import from existing-session profile into managed openclaw profile

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit one-shot import that copies a same-user existing-session browser profile into a managed OpenClaw browser profile, and what consent and safe-copy limits are required?
rationale: The implementation shape is reasonably clear, but copying signed-in personal browser state into managed agent storage changes a security and privacy boundary that automation should not choose on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept explicit guarded import
options.body: Implement a one-shot browser-plugin import that requires explicit user intent, stops/resets the destination, strips transient files, leaves the source untouched, and documents the security implications.

options.title: Decline profile copying
options.body: Keep managed profiles isolated and direct users to existing-session mode when they need signed-in state, avoiding a new copy of personal browser data into agent storage.

options.title: Defer for broader policy
options.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers define a broader browser profile ownership and data-copying policy.

recommendation.title: Accept explicit guarded import
recommendation.body: Implement a one-shot browser-plugin import that requires explicit user intent, stops/resets the destination, strips transient files, leaves the source untouched, and documents the security implications.
